newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs dying as winter energy crisis bites.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs dying as winter energy crisis bites.

text.p: A heating gas shortage has forced many Kazakhs to experiment this winter with potentially lethal home-made heaters, emergency services officials said on Tuesday.

Toxic fumes killed a family of four in Zyryanovsk in the east of the former Soviet republic on Monday after the electrical wiring in their apartment began to smoulder during the night, the state emergencies committee said. On the same day, a child died in a gas blast in another region.
"Low temperatures in apartments are leading to a widespread use of home-made heaters which often either burst into flames or cause electrical fires," spokesman Valery Yemelin told Reuters.
"There are daily explosions caused by frequent interruptions of the gas supply to residential areas and even whole towns," he added.

The official newspaper Kazakhstanskaya Pravda said on Tuesday that in Kokshetau in northern Kazakhstan "schools, hospitals, kindergartens and businesses are all prisoners of the ice" as heating systems went down in temperatures of minus 30 degress Celsius (-22 Fahrenheit).
